stanzas.sanskrit:
रुचिरकम्पितकुण्डलमण्डलः
सुचिरमीश ननर्तिथ पन्नगे ।
अमरताडितदुन्दुभिसुन्दरं
वियति गायति दैवतयौवते ॥ ५६-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna danced on the hoods of Kaaliya for a long time according to the tunes of musical sounds made by the Devas along with His ear drops dancing.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
rucirakampitakuṇḍalamaṇḍalaḥ
suciramīśa nanartitha pannage |
amaratāḍitadundubhisundaraṃ
viyati gāyati daivatayauvate || 56-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
नमति यद्यदमुष्य शिरो हरे
परिविहाय तदुन्नतमुन्नतम् ।
परिमथन् पदपङ्करुहा चिरं
व्यहरथाः करतालमनोहरम् ॥ ५६-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna played around for long time, jumping on the raised hoods one after the other, leaving the ones which dropped down, clapping hands beautifully in rhythm.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
namati yadyadamuṣya śiro hare
parivihāya tadunnatamunnatam |
parimathan padapaṅkaruhā ciraṃ
vyaharathāḥ karatālamanoharam || 56-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वदवभग्नविभुग्नफणागणे
गलितशोणितशोणितपाथसि ।
फणिपताववसीदति सन्नता-
-स्तदबलास्तव माधव पादयोः ॥ ५६-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
The hoods were getting crushed under Krishna's feet and soon Kaaliya became tired. The blood flowing from them made the waters of the river Yamuna red.
When all the hoods started exhausting, the serpent wives surrendered at the feet of Bhagwan.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvadavabhagnavibhugnaphaṇāgaṇe
galitaśoṇitaśoṇitapāthasi |
phaṇipatāvavasīdati sannatā-
-stadabalāstava mādhava pādayoḥ || 56-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अयि पुरैव चिराय परिश्रुत-
-त्वदनुभावविलीनहृदो हि ताः ।
मुनिभिरप्यनवाप्यपथैः स्तवै-
-र्नुनुवुरीश भवन्तमयन्त्रितम् ॥ ५६-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The serpent wives very well knew about Bhagwan’s majestic greatness. Their minds were absorbed in Bhagwan and sang praises which were not even sung by great sages.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ayi puraiva cirāya pariśruta-
-tvadanubhāvavilīnahṛdo hi tāḥ |
munibhirapyanavāpyapathaiḥ stavai-
-rnunuvurīśa bhavantamayantritam || 56-4 ||

stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan’s heart was overflowing with compassion on seeing the devotion of the serpent wives. Krishna took his feet off Kaaliya, who immediately surrendered to Bhagwan at along with his wives.

stanzas.sanskrit:
रमणकं व्रज वारिधिमध्यगं
फणिरिपुर्न करोति विरोधिताम् ।
इति भवद्वचनान्यतिमानयन्
फणिपतिर्निरगादुरगैः समम् ॥ ५६-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna directed Kaaliya to go to Ramanaka Island, situated in the middle of the ocean and promised that he will not be disturbed by Garuda there. Respecting the words of Krishna, Kaaliya left to Ramanaka island with his wives immediately.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ramaṇakaṃ vraja vāridhimadhyagaṃ
phaṇiripurna karoti virodhitām |
iti bhavadvacanānyatimānayan
phaṇipatirniragāduragaiḥ samam || 56-6 ||

stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna dressed himself with the precious gems and jewels gifted by the wives of Kaaliya and reached the shore by the evening. Gopas greeted Krishna with tears of joy.

stanzas.sanskrit:
निशि पुनस्तमसा व्रजमन्दिरं
व्रजितुमक्षम एव जनोत्करे ।
स्वपति तत्र भवच्चरणाश्रये
दवकृशानुररुन्ध समन्ततः ॥ ५६-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
It became dark and hence, Krishna and Gopas could not return to Vraja. They decided to stay back in the forest at night.
Gopas were sleeping on the banks of the river holding Krishna's feet. A forest fire engulfed them at the middle of night on all four sides.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
niśi punastamasā vrajamandiraṃ
vrajitumakṣama eva janotkare |
svapati tatra bhavaccaraṇāśraye
davakṛśānurarundha samantataḥ || 56-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रबुधितानथ पालय पालये-
-त्युदयदार्तरवान् पशुपालकान् ।
अवितुमाशु पपाथ महानलं
किमिह चित्रमयं खलु ते मुखम् ॥ ५६-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopas awakened by the forest fire, cried to Krishna for help. Krishna drank the fire to protect the gopas. It is no surprise as Bhagwan’s face itself is agni.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prabudhitānatha pālaya pālaye-
-tyudayadārtaravān paśupālakān |
avitumāśu papātha mahānalaṃ
kimiha citramayaṃ khalu te mukham || 56-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
शिखिनि वर्णत एव हि पीतता
परिलसत्यधुना क्रिययाऽप्यसौ ।
इति नुतः पशुपैर्मुदितैर्विभो
हर हरे दुरितैः सह मे गदान् ॥ ५६-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Gopas appreciated the fact that earlier, the Peethathvam or yellowness was only found in agni or fire as colour, but now due to His action, it can be perfectly called Peethathvam (act of drinking in the verb form).
Bhattathiri prayed to Lord Guruvayoorappan to remove his sins and afflictions.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śikhini varṇata eva hi pītatā
parilasatyadhunā kriyayā’pyasau |
iti nutaḥ paśupairmuditairvibho
hara hare duritaiḥ saha me gadān || 56-10 ||
